known.text: A software company in Newcastle, NSW, helping wholesalers since 2010
Main product: an iPad sales app for wholesale reps, with a digital catalogue, order taking in the field, a CRM that suggests which client to visit next, and sales reports
Also an iPhone Lite version, an online store and customer order portals
Connects to customers' accounting and business systems, including MYOB and Cin7
New customers come through a free demo, then a guided onboarding, then a customer success team
Promises real human support, not a chat-bot
Says reps' sales go up 26% on average
What Dan has already discussed with them
Brand feel from the site: clean, light, blue-leaning, plain-spoken
Accent colour is a placeholder blue. Swap in their exact brand colour
No logo added yet. Add the web address of the logo on their site

opening: From your site I've got that Inzant is a mobile sales platform for wholesale reps, based in Newcastle, with integrations into accounting and ERP tools. Is that still the right picture?

winning: Your site pushes a free demo. Walk me through what happens from the moment someone asks for one to the moment they say yes or no. Which part do you wish someone else did?
Every demo is probably tailored to the wholesaler's range and systems. What do you prepare each time, and how long does it take?
Where do leads sit while they wait on a reply from you?
doing: Every new customer gets a guided onboarding. List the steps from signing to a rep using the app. Which step always takes longer than it should?
Each customer's product range has to get into the catalogue. How does it arrive, in what format, and who cleans it up?
You integrate with accounting and ERP systems like MYOB and Cin7. What goes wrong most often with a new integration, and who fixes it?
What do your support staff answer over and over? Give me the five questions you'd love to never type again.
Walk me through the last support issue that took longer than a day.
running: How do you find out something broke before a customer rings you?
What do you do every Monday morning that nobody has written down?
You promise real humans, not a chat-bot. What's the one job your team does by hand that you'd gladly give to AI without losing that promise?
How do you report on the sales lift you claim, and who builds that for each customer?
connections: When you use AI, how does it see your customer data, support tickets or product notes: pasted in, or connected?
Which of your tools can't an AI read at all: support inbox, code, customer records, billing?
Think of the last time AI got something about your business wrong. What did it not know?
gaps: Which other mobile sales platform do prospects mention? What do they do that quietly bothers you that you don't?
If you started on that tomorrow, how would you go about it, and what's stopping you?
What would you do with two spare days a week?

marketing.text: Wholesalers searching for a mobile sales app are probably comparing a few platforms. Do you know where Inzant shows up when they do, and has anything been tried to show up higher?
How are your ads doing today? What have you tried before, what worked, and where did you get burned?
What marketing has actually brought in good customers, and what looked promising but wasted money?
Where have you been burned by an agency or a freelancer?
Which channel do you feel you should be doing more of?
